mainTopic: Blood mixtures: when blood is cancelled for קרבנות and כיסוי, שמואל's 'reddish look' rule, blood plasma, and the liquids of a מת
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about blood that needs כיסוי הדם getting mixed with other blood, where רבי יהודה says blood never cancels blood. The משנה then rules that spurted blood and blood on the knife must be covered, and רבי יהודה limits this to when no other blood is there. The גמרא quotes a matching משנה in זבחים about sacrificial blood mixed with water, wine, or other blood. רבי יוחנן says that משנה applies only when water fell into blood; if blood fell into water, each drop is cancelled as it lands. רב פפא adds that for כיסוי this cancelling is not permanent, since there is no דחוי for מצוות. שמואל teaches that any reddish mixture counts as blood for atonement, הכשר, and כיסוי, and the גמרא works out that his new point is about rainwater that fell into blood by itself. Later אמוראים and a ברייתא apply this to blood plasma: it can make food susceptible, eating it carries כרת, and from a מת it is מטמא באהל. Finally, the גמרא quotes a teaching that a מת's liquids are טהור except blood, and begins to challenge it from a משנה about a טבול יום, a challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blood mixed with other blood: treat it like water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its list of mixtures. If blood that needs covering got mixed with blood that does not, we picture the other blood as water. רבי יהודה disagrees: blood never cancels out blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it got mixed with the blood of a wild animal that does not need covering, we picture that blood as if it were water. רבי יהודה says: blood does not cancel out blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rule about blood that needs כיסוי getting mixed with other blood. The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה disagree about whether the other blood can cancel it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא asks one question: would this blood still look like blood if the other blood were plain water? If not, it is cancelled and needs no covering. רבי יהודה holds that blood cannot cancel blood, so the mixture must always be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: We view it as though; we picture the mixed-in liquid as something else
Blood does not cancel out blood
Cancellation; a small amount loses its identity inside a larger mixture
The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered wild animal or bird

phrases.english: or with the blood of a wild animal
phrases.notes: The start of this case is on the previous page: blood that must be covered got mixed with blood that need not be covered.

phrases.english: we view it as though it were water.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Blood does not cancel out blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, other blood is pictured as water when deciding whether the mixture still needs covering. According to רבי יהודה, blood never cancels blood.

steps.title: Spurted blood and blood on the knife must be covered
steps.stepSummary: Blood that spurted away from the main spot, and blood left on the knife, still has to be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood that spurts out, and blood that is on the knife, must be covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule: blood that did not land in the usual place still carries the obligation of כיסוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think only the main pool of blood needs covering. The משנה says that any blood from the שחיטה is included, even blood that spurted aside or stuck to the knife.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that spurts or splashes away from the main spot
The slaughtering knife
Obligated to cover

phrases.english: Blood that spurts out, and blood that is on the knife,
one is obligated to cover it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spurted blood and blood on the knife must be covered.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the rule about spurted blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the obligation applies only when no other blood from the שחיטה is left. If other blood is there, this blood does not need covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? When no blood is left there except this blood. But if there is other blood there besides it, one is exempt from covering it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה narrows the rule from the last step. The spurted blood or the blood on the knife needs covering only when it is all the blood there is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's view, the מצוה is done by covering the main blood. Extra splashes need covering only when nothing else is available to cover.

keyTerms.meaning: When? Introduces a limit on an earlier rule
Exempt from covering

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When does this apply?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין שָׁם דָּם אֶלָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: When there is no blood there except that blood.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ שָׁם דָּם שֶׁלֹּא הוּא –
phrases.english: But if there is blood there other than it,
one is exempt from covering it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If other blood from the שחיטה is present, spurted blood or blood on the knife does not need covering.

steps.title: The matching משנה in זבחים about sacrificial blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in זבחים. Sacrificial blood mixed with water is still fit if it looks like blood. Wine or other blood is pictured as water, and רבי יהודה again says blood does not cancel blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Blood that got mixed with water is fit if it still looks like blood. If it got mixed with wine, we picture the wine as water. If it got mixed with the blood of a domestic or wild animal, we picture that blood as water. רבי יהודה says: blood does not cancel out blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a parallel משנה from זבחים that uses the same rules as our משנה. It is setting up a teaching of רבי יוחנן about that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same test is used for sacrificial blood: does the mixture still look like blood? Wine and ordinary blood are red, so we cannot judge by how they look. That is why we picture them as water. רבי יהודה's view that blood never cancels blood shows up here too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
There; in a different place in the ש״ס
The appearance of blood
Fit; here, fit to be sprinkled on the מזבח
Became mixed

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
Blood that got mixed with water,
phrases.notes: This is blood of a קרבן that is meant to be sprinkled on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מַרְאִית דָּם – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: if it has the appearance of blood, it is fit.
If it got mixed with wine,
we view it as though it were water.

phrases.aramaic: נִתְעָרֵב בְּדַם בְּהֵמָה אוֹ בְּדַם הַחַיָּה –
phrases.english: If it got mixed with the blood of a domestic animal or the blood of a wild animal,
phrases.notes: This is ordinary blood that is not from a קרבן.

phrases.english: we view it as though it were water.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין דָּם מְבַטֵּל דָּם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Blood does not cancel out blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא brings a parallel משנה to set up a discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sacrificial blood mixed with water is fit if it still looks like blood. Red liquids mixed in are pictured as water.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only when water fell into blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה's rule (fit if it looks like blood) applies only when water fell into the blood. If blood fell into water, each drop is cancelled the moment it lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this only when water fell into blood. But if blood fell into water, each first drop is cancelled as it falls.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits the זבחים משנה. Its "looks like blood" test works only when the water is poured into the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When water falls into blood, the blood was there first and is never outnumbered drop by drop. When blood drips into water, every single drop lands in much more water and is cancelled right away. So the mixture is unfit even if it later turns red.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of; a phrase that limits a ruling
Each first drop is cancelled; every drop is cancelled as it falls in
Fell into

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the only question is what the mixture looks like at the end. According to רבי יוחנן, the order matters: which liquid fell into which.
steps.whatToRemember: Water into blood: fit if it looks like blood. Blood into water: ראשון ראשון בטל, so the blood is cancelled drop by drop.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step, where רב פפא explains that the "which fell into which" rule does not work the same way for our משנה about כיסוי הדם.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
They taught this only
when water fell into blood.
But if blood fell into water,
each first drop is cancelled.
phrases.notes: He means each drop is cancelled in the water as soon as it lands, one after another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּפְלוּ מַיִם לְתוֹךְ דָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה quoted in the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The "looks like blood" test applies only when water fell into blood. When blood falls into water, each drop is cancelled as it lands.

steps.title: For covering blood, being pushed aside is not permanent
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits רבי יוחנן's rule. For כיסוי הדם, blood that fell into water is not cancelled forever, because there is no permanent דחוי when it comes to מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: But for the מצוה of covering the blood, it is not like that. There is no permanent pushing aside when it comes to מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a limit to what רבי יוחנן said in step 5. The rule that blood falling into water is cancelled drop by drop applies to קדשים, not to כיסוי הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, each drop of sacrificial blood falling into water was cancelled the moment it landed, and it stayed cancelled. רב פפא says that for כיסוי, the cancelling is only temporary. Once the mixture looks like blood again, the obligation to cover comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Being 'pushed aside': something becomes disqualified and stays that way.
For (non-sacrificial) מצוות, something that was pushed aside can come back.
The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא is arguing with רבי יוחנן. He agrees about קרבנות. He is only saying the rule works differently for כיסוי.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
But regarding covering, it is not so,
phrases.notes: He means: for covering, blood that fell into water is not cancelled for good, unlike the sacrificial blood in step 5.

phrases.english: there is no rejection with regard to מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וּלְעִנְיַן כִּסּוּי אֵינוֹ כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי יוחנן's drop-by-drop cancellation to קדשים, and shows it does not apply to כיסוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For כיסוי הדם, blood that fell into water is not permanently cancelled. Once the mixture looks like blood, it must be covered.

steps.title: Any reddish mixture counts as blood in three ways
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quoting שמואל: any mixture that looks reddish atones, makes food susceptible to טומאה, and needs covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: anything with a reddish look atones, makes food able to become טמא, and must be covered.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic. שמואל gives one test for blood mixtures, which is whether it still looks reddish, and applies it to three different areas of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is simply how the mixture looks. If it is still reddish, it is treated as blood for קרבנות (atonement), for הכשר (making food susceptible), and for כיסוי הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: A reddish look, which shows the mixture still counts as blood.
They atone, when the blood is put on the מזבח.
They make food susceptible, meaning able to become טמא.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:
Any reddish appearance –
effects atonement, and renders food susceptible,
phrases.notes: Food can only become טמא after a liquid like water or blood has gotten it wet; that's what 'renders susceptible' means.

phrases.english: and requires covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל מַרְאֵה אַדְּמוּמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement about blood mixtures, related to the topic of steps 4–6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A reddish mixture counts as blood for atonement, for הכשר, and for כיסוי.

steps.title: Why say this? Two of the rules are already in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל adds. Atonement is already taught in the משנה in זבחים, and covering is already taught in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That it atones, we already learned. That it must be covered, we already learned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's statement as unnecessary, because two of his three points are already found in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4's משנה in זבחים says blood mixed with water that looks like blood is fit, so it atones. Our own משנה (its earlier part, on the previous page) already says blood mixed with water that still looks like blood must be covered. So what new point did שמואל make?

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? This asks what new point a statement adds.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That it effects atonement – we already learned,
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה in זבחים from step 4.

phrases.english: that it requires covering – we already learned!
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה, in the part on the previous page about blood mixed with water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 7 as adding nothing new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching that only repeats a משנה is unnecessary. Two of its three points are already in a משנה.

steps.title: The new point is 'makes food susceptible'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל needed to teach מכשירין, which no משנה says.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed to teach that it makes food susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The new part of שמואל's statement is the rule about making food susceptible to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Atonement and covering are already known. So the reason שמואל spoke up must be the middle rule, מכשירין, since no משנה teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him to say this.

phrases.english: Rendering susceptible was necessary for him to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by pointing to the one rule not yet taught.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the new detail in the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's whole statement seemed to repeat known משניות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The new point is that the mixture counts for הכשר.

steps.title: Either way it makes food susceptible, so why say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Blood makes food susceptible, and water does too, so it should not matter what the mixture counts as.
steps.simpleTranslation: Making food susceptible is also obvious! If it is blood, it makes food susceptible. If it is water, it makes food susceptible too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Even the מכשירין rule seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood and water are both liquids that make food susceptible to טומאה. So whether the reddish mixture counts as blood or as water, the result is the same, and שמואל's rule changes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If this… if that…': whichever way you look at it, the result is the same.
Water.

phrases.english: Rendering susceptible is also obvious,
if it is blood – it renders susceptible,
if it is water – it renders susceptible!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מכשירין is the new teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both blood and water make food susceptible, so calling the mixture blood makes no practical difference.

steps.title: The case is blood mixed with rainwater
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed where the blood mixed with rainwater. Rainwater does not always make food susceptible, so it matters that the mixture counts as blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where it was mixed with rainwater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding a case where it does make a difference whether the mixture counts as blood: rainwater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rainwater on its own does not make food susceptible unless someone wanted it there. So if the mixture counted as water, it might not make food susceptible. שמואל teaches that because it looks reddish, it counts as blood and does.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for a specific case.
Rainwater.
That it was mixed (diluted) with.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where it was mixed with rainwater.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by finding a case where blood and water are treated differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood and water always both make food susceptible, so the rule changes nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: With rainwater, only the 'blood' status makes the food susceptible.

steps.title: Putting rainwater in on purpose makes it count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. If someone took rainwater and poured it into the blood, he showed he wants it, so it would make food susceptible anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rainwater too: since he took it and poured it in, he gave it importance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rainwater case. Pouring the rainwater in on purpose already makes it count as wanted water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rainwater makes food susceptible once a person wants it. Taking it and putting it into the blood shows he wanted it. Then it makes food susceptible even as water, so the rule is again unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes it and throws (pours) it in.
He treated them as important, which shows he wants them.

phrases.english: Rainwater as well,
since he took it and poured it in,
he has given it importance.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵי גְשָׁמִים נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁקֵיל וְרָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rainwater case of step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pouring the rainwater in on purpose shows the person wanted it, so the water itself makes food susceptible anyway.

steps.title: The rainwater got mixed in by itself
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed where the rainwater mixed into the blood on its own, with no one putting it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where they got mixed by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final, narrowest case. The rain fell into the blood without anyone doing anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no one poured the rainwater in, no one showed he wanted it. As water, it would not make food susceptible. Only because the reddish mixture counts as blood does it make food susceptible, and that is שמואל's new teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: By themselves, with no person's action.
They became mixed.

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a mixture that still looks reddish counts as blood. His new point is that it makes food susceptible even when rainwater fell into the blood by itself, where water alone would not.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where they were mixed by themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by narrowing the case further.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rainwater put in by a person already counts as wanted, so the rule adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the rain fell in by itself, only the 'blood' status makes the food susceptible.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's rule teaches that a reddish mixture of blood and rainwater that fell in by itself makes food susceptible, because it counts as blood.

steps.title: The rule refers to blood plasma
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי of נהרביל says the earlier rule about a mixture that still looks like blood is talking about blood plasma.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי of נהרביל says: this is talking about blood plasma.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא tells us what real-life case the earlier rule of שמואל, quoted by רב יהודה, is describing. He says it is the watery liquid of blood, called plasma.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule in step 7, defended in steps 8 to 13, said that a reddish mixture still counts as blood. רבי אסי gives a natural example: the clear liquid that separates from blood. If it still has a reddish look, it has the status of blood and can make food מוכשר לקבל טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood plasma, the clear watery liquid that separates from blood
Making food able to become טמא by wetting it with certain liquids

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi of Neharbil says:
It refers to blood plasma.
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to the rule that a mixture with a reddish look still counts as blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete case for the rule defended in steps 9 to 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood plasma with a reddish look counts as blood for making food מוכשר

steps.title: Eating plasma can carry the punishment of כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה of דפתי adds that eating this plasma carries כרת, as long as there is a כזית of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה of דפתי said: one who eats it is punished with כרת, as long as there is an olive-sized amount.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא adds another law about the same blood plasma. Eating it is like eating blood, which is punished with כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plasma counts as blood for more than just making food מוכשר. It also counts as blood for the איסור of eating blood. The limit is that there must be a full כזית of actual blood in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Punished with כרת, being cut off spiritually, the punishment for eating blood
An olive-sized amount, the minimum amount of eating that is punishable
Provided that there is, a condition that limits the rule

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti said:
One who eats it is punished with karet,
provided that there is an olive-bulk.
phrases.notes: He means an olive-bulk of actual blood inside the plasma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second law about the plasma defined in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating blood plasma is punished with כרת if it has a כזית of blood

steps.title: Plasma from a dead body makes a tent טמא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that plasma from a מת is מטמא באהל, as long as there is a רביעית of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: it makes things טמא in a tent, as long as there is a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a third law about plasma. Plasma that comes from a dead body spreads טומאה under a roof, just like the blood of a מת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, plasma is treated like blood, this time for טומאת מת. Here the needed amount is a רביעית of actual blood, because that is the amount of a מת's blood that is מטמא באהל.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים left out of the משנה
Spread טומאה to people and things under the same roof
A quarter-לוג, the amount of a מת's blood that spreads טומאה in a tent

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
They impart impurity in a tent,
phrases.notes: This is talking about reddish plasma that comes from a dead body.

phrases.english: provided that there is a quarter-log.

steps.whatToRemember: Plasma with a reddish look is treated as blood in three areas: הכשר, כרת for eating it with a כזית, and טומאת אהל with a רביעית.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third law about blood plasma, this time from a ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plasma from a מת is מטמא באהל if it contains a רביעית of blood

steps.title: Liquids from a dead body are טהור except its blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching: all liquids from a מת are טהור except its blood, and anything with a reddish look is מטמא באהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned elsewhere: all liquids of a dead body are טהור, except its blood. And any liquid from it with a reddish look makes things טמא in a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a teaching about the liquids of a מת. It is setting this up so it can question it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquids like tears that come from a dead body are טהור. Only blood, or a liquid that has a reddish look of blood in it, is מטמא באהל. This fits the idea from step 16 that reddish liquid counts as blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids that come out of a dead body, like tears
A reddish look, showing that blood is mixed in

phrases.english: We learned elsewhere:
All liquids of a corpse are pure,
except for its blood,
and every liquid from it that has a reddish look
imparts impurity in a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related teaching about liquids of a מת, linked by the idea of a reddish look
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liquids from a מת are טהור except blood and anything with a reddish look

steps.title: Can a dead body's liquids really be טהור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the teaching and begins a contradiction from the law of a טבול יום, whose liquids are like liquids he touches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are liquids of a dead body really טהור? Raise a contradiction: the liquids of a טבול יום, the liquids that come out of him, are like liquids that he touches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a dead body's liquids could be טהור. It starts to bring a משנה about a טבול יום to show the opposite, and the challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום is someone who went to the מקוה today but is waiting for nightfall to be fully טהור. The משנה says the liquids that come out of him, like saliva, have the same status as liquids he touches. The quote goes on, on the next amud, to give the same rule for every other kind of טמא person, including the most severe ones. That is what clashes with the teaching that a מת's liquids are טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today and is waiting for nightfall to be fully טהור

phrases.english: But are the liquids of a corpse pure?
And raise a contradiction:
The liquids of one who immersed that day,
the liquids that come out of him
are like liquids that he touches,
phrases.notes: So his own liquids share the status of liquids he touches. The rest of the quote comes next.

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that all liquids of a מת are טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about a טבול יום goes on, on the next amud, to say that for all other טמאים, severe ones too, liquids coming out of them have the same status as liquids they touch. That would make a מת's liquids טמא, which contradicts the teaching that they are טהור.
